extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners conducting or appraising systematic reviews in public health/child protection (health professionals, policymakers, child-protection researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: A preregistered systematic review protocol (OSF) following PRISMA 2020, investigating determinants of underreporting of violence against children with emphasis on health professionals' self-efficacy and relevance for low- and middle-income countries (esp. Angola).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to PRISMA 2020 guidelines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol claims compliance with PRISMA 2020 for systematic review reporting; reviewers should expect PRISMA-aligned sections (search strategy, selection process, data extraction, risk of bias, synthesis) and assess completeness of reporting against PRISMA items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, focused research scope on underreporting and self-efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic review protocol investigating determinants of underreporting of violence against children, with emphasis on the self-efficacy of health professionals in recognizing and reporting suspected abuse cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The protocol should define inclusion/exclusion criteria, populations, exposures (determinants), outcomes (underreporting, reporting behaviour), and how self-efficacy is measured or operationalized. Relevance to health professionals' recognition/reporting practices should be explicit in eligibility and synthesis plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and applicability to public health policy and practice (LMIC focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims to provide evidence for public health policies, professional training, and child protection systems, with relevance for low- and middle-income countries, especially Angola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer should assess whether study selection, subgroup analyses, and contextualization of findings address applicability to LMIC settings and to policy/practice implications (e.g., recommendations for training, system changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science and preregistration (OSF registration and licensing)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSF preregistration provided (Osf_registration_doi: 10.17605/OSF.IO/XCYRM) and licensed under CC BY 4.0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol is registered on OSF and uses an open license; reviewers should verify that the preregistered protocol matches planned analyses and that deviations are documented. Open licensing supports reuse and transparency.
